h1: Packaging Mockup Generator for a Shelf or Cafe Scene
lead: A packaging mockup generator makes a preview picture, not the printed pack. Make it for a shelf, counter, or cafe from one photo of the pouch, box, or bottle. If that photo also becomes a video, add a spoken voice and words on screen. Credits, what each job spends, are shown before you start.

steps_h2: Make a Shelf Preview from One Package Photo in 3 Steps
steps_lead: One photo of the real package, one scene, then a square file you compare with a sample print.

faq.q: What is a packaging mockup generator?
faq.a: A square shelf, counter, or cafe preview from one photo of the pouch, box, or bottle you will ship. It shows how the pack sits in the scene, not print color or legal words. That photo can also start a video with an AI actor, a script (the words), and a voiceover (a spoken voice).

faq.q: How does the preview get made?
faq.a: Upload the package photo or paste a product page link, name the shelf scene, and download the square file. For a video, add the script, the spoken voice, and words on screen in the editor.

faq.q: Why use this instead of filming a creator?
faq.a: You can judge how the shelf looks before a print order, and make a product video without booking a creator. A sample print still checks color and small legal words.
Food, drink, beauty, and home shops, plus agencies. Use it for slides for a store buyer, a listing idea, or a product video.
Yes. One clear photo of the full package is enough. You do not need an editing background to set captions, music, or a spoken line on the clip.
Pouches, cartons, bottles, tins, jars, and bags work when the package shape is visible in the source photo. A pouch packaging mockup and a coffee packaging mockup both start that way.

faq.q: Can I upload my own pack photo?
faq.a: Yes. The photo of the package you will ship is the source. A design file by itself is not. A box mockup from a design photo still needs that real package in the frame.

faq.q: Where can I use the file?
faq.a: The square preview fits a listing idea, slides, or a post. A video from the same photo can go to TikTok, Instagram, Facebook, YouTube, or Shopify. Shapes are 9:16 (tall), 1:1 (square), 16:9 (wide), 4:3, and 3:4 (tall).

faq.q: Do I need a paid plan?
faq.a: Yes. There is no free plan. Plans start at $24.50 a month. The square preview is 24 credits. Credits are what the job spends. A video is 24, 40, 60, or 120 credits for 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. You see the cost first, and a failed job returns its credits. The download has no watermark, nothing stamped on the file.

faq.q: Can I use the preview in a pitch or an ad?
faq.a: Yes. Use it in your store, in slides for a store buyer, or in an ad. It does not replace a sample print when color or tiny print must be exact. Any person in a video is an AI actor, not a buyer.

faq.q: Why start from a shelf scene instead of a blank frame?
faq.a: The shelf, counter, or cafe scene is already set, so you can compare versions faster. You can still make a second opening line, speak another language, or use the API so your product list starts the next pack.

items.t: A finished shelf frame from one pack photo

items.t: The mockup and a clip in one project

items.d: Example: the pouch stays the shelf picture. On the video, the shop picks an AI actor, a generated person, then adds words on screen.

items.t: The same jar scene in another language
items.d: Example: the wood-shelf still stays as it is, and the spoken line on the clip is recorded again for a second market.

items.t: A voiceover and a track on the clip
items.d: Example: the carton preview is for slides you show a store buyer. On the video, the editor adds a spoken voice and a track from the music library.

items.t: An AI actor instead of a filmed spot
items.d: Example: a supplement shop uses an AI actor, a generated person, to hold the pack. Small ingredient text can blur, so the real label photo keeps the wording.

items.t: A digital twin for the next bag
items.d: Example: a pet-food shop uses a digital twin, the same generated person, so the next bag clip matches the first. No new light setup.

items.t: A script, then a second version
items.d: Example: a juice shop pastes the product link, takes a short script, and compares two bottle versions in the same scene.

items.t: Publish the clip, or start from the API
items.d: Example: after a look at the sample print, the shop posts the clip to TikTok or Meta (Facebook and Instagram). The API lets the product list start the next box.
